# Implementation Plan: Native Anthropic Messages (`/v1/messages`) transport for signed chain-of-thought
<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"codex-anthropic-native-messages-transport-for-signed-cot"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-26. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan .ralph/jobs/codex-anthropic-native-messages-transport-for-signed-cot/plan.md`.*

## Overview

The fork already routes Claude-via-Copilot over a fork-exclusive `/chat/completions` transport (D-001 `WireApi::ChatCompletions`). That path now also captures, persists and replays Claude chain-of-thought (CoT) — but as **unsigned plaintext**, because Copilot streams CoT as a non-standard `choices[].delta.reasoning_text` carrying no signature (sibling task `codex-anthropic-chat-reasoning-text-capture-and-replay`, shipped on `origin/main`). This plan adds a **third transport** that talks the native Anthropic Messages API (`POST api.githubcopilot.com/v1/messages`) so Claude's CoT round-trips as **signed `thinking` blocks** (`thinking` + cryptographic `signature`) across the tool loop — the faithful continuity the unsigned path cannot deliver.

The work is **probe-gated** (brainstorm direction D-001). Even though an earlier feasibility probe returned GO, the plan **front-loads a confirmation re-probe** (US-001) of three gates — (a) Copilot bearer auth accepted on `/v1/messages`, (b) signed `thinking`+`signature` emitted, (c) a replayed signed `thinking` block accepted before a `tool_result` on a 2nd turn — and **no codex-rs transport code lands until that probe re-confirms GO**. On NO-GO the plan falls back to D-003 (defer/abandon; unsigned plaintext replay stands). Because the unsigned sibling shipped first and deliberately froze the extension points (the `encrypted_content` signature slot, the unchanged reasoning lifecycle, the never-stripped `encrypted_content` on replay), the signed path **extends** those shapes rather than colliding with them — the previously-feared `anthropic_sse.rs` + `payload.rs` parallel-edit conflict is moot.

This is a **codex-submodule** effort, overlay-first per the fork's engineering tenets. The minimal upstream-canonical edit set is four enum/routing seams plus one dispatch arm; the bulk (the Anthropic Messages request builder) lives in a new overlay file. It is a **nested 2-repo change**: Rust code in the inner submodule (`codex/external/repos/codex-patched/`) plus the patch-surface ledger in the codex wrapper (`codex/docs/implementation/patch-surface.md`) — a two-commit flow (inner first, then wrapper pointer bump).

## Approach

### Architecture

Add a **third wire**, `WireApi::AnthropicMessages` (route `ModelWireRoute::AnthropicMessages`), selected for a Claude row that advertises `/v1/messages` **only when a stricter signed sub-flag is on**. The signed path reuses the existing Copilot auth/headers/billing (`CopilotHeaderSource`/`CopilotAuth`, same `api.githubcopilot.com` host + token cache), the existing `AnthropicSseParser` (extended to surface the signature), and the existing reasoning persistence lifecycle (extended to carry the signature in the already-reserved `encrypted_content` slot). The one genuinely new body of code is the **outbound Anthropic Messages request builder**, which lives in a new overlay file.

Three load-bearing design decisions (resolved here; revisited in Phase-4 review):

1. **Stricter sub-flag, default off, single resolver.** Add `Feature::AnthropicSignedMessages` (key `anthropic_signed_messages`, `default_enabled:false`) ANDed with `AnthropicModels`. Rationale: the signed path is unvalidated against the proxy; reusing `anthropic_models` would expose unproven behavior to everyone who enabled Claude. A separate gate lets signed ship dark while the unsigned chat path stays the Claude default until a soak window validates replay acceptance. Matches the fork's experimental-features convention. To avoid drift, expose a **single** `install_anthropic_signed_messages_gate(enabled)` / `anthropic_signed_messages_resolved()` pair in `model-provider/src/anthropic_gate.rs` (mirroring the existing `install_anthropic_gate`/`anthropic_models_resolved` pair at `:37-45`, re-exported from `model-provider/src/lib.rs:24-25`) and read it at EVERY site whose behavior changes: `wire_route_for`, the model-cache identity, the `GatedModelsManager` visibility filter, and `synthesize_from_capabilities`. The flag is **installed at config-build time** in `core/src/config/mod.rs` alongside `install_anthropic_gate` — without that install path the flag stays `false`.

2. **Graceful degrade, never panic; routing-arm and dispatch-stub both safe in US-002.** `effective_wire_api_gated` gains an `AnthropicMessages` arm that maps to `WireApi::AnthropicMessages` only when the signed flag is on; otherwise it **degrades to `WireApi::ChatCompletions`** (the shipped unsigned path). Crucially, to keep the US-002 skeleton truly inert even if an operator flips the flag early, **US-002 keeps the degrade unconditional** (always → `ChatCompletions`) and the US-002 `client.rs` dispatch stub **delegates to `stream_chat_completions`** (runs unsigned, never panics); **US-005** is the only story that flips `effective_wire_api_gated` to honor the signed flag and replaces the stub with the real `stream_anthropic_messages` driver. This removes the "flag-on before the driver exists breaks the model path" hazard. The signed flag is threaded into `effective_wire_api_gated` as an **explicit parameter** (mirroring the existing `anthropic_enabled: bool` arg at `:68-72`) so the degrade-vs-route decision stays unit-testable without process-global state; the resolver read happens only at the `effective_wire_api` wrapper (`:64-66`).

3. **Extend the existing core SSE parser; do NOT duplicate it in the overlay.** `anthropic_sse.rs` already parses the Anthropic Messages envelope (`message_start`/`content_block_*`/`message_delta`) and only drops `thinking_delta`/`signature_delta` at `:179-181`. It is a fork-exclusive D-001 file already plumbed into the chat run path, so extending it adds ~zero new upstream conflict surface and avoids re-implementing the envelope parser. (Alternative considered: a new overlay `messages_sse.rs` — pure overlay but duplicates the envelope parsing. Rejected for duplication; noted in Open Questions for Phase-4 reviewers to confirm.)

### Implementation Strategy (ordered)

0. **US-001 — Confirmation re-probe (GATE, first, no codex edits).** Extend the external probe; on GO proceed, on NO-GO halt to D-003.
1. **US-002 — Routing skeleton + signed sub-flag (upstream seams, inert).** Third `WireApi`/`ModelWireRoute` arm, `/v1/messages` recognition, `effective_wire_api` arm with degrade-to-chat, sub-flag Feature + resolver, a dispatch stub arm. Compiles independently; degrade-to-chat keeps it inert.
2. **US-003 — Inbound signed-SSE capture + signature persistence (core).** Surface `thinking_delta`/`signature_delta`; persist the signature into `encrypted_content`.
3. **US-004 — Outbound Anthropic Messages request builder (overlay, the bulk).** New overlay file; signed `thinking`→`tool_use`→`tool_result` ordering; byte-cap including signature.
4. **US-005 — Dispatch wiring + signed round-trip (core join).** Replace the US-002 stub with the real `WireApi::AnthropicMessages` arm + `stream_anthropic_messages` driver; signed round-trip integration test across the tool loop.
5. **US-006 — Harden, audit, verify.** Network-audit allowlist (Invariant 38 + `audit_network_calls.sh`) for `/v1/messages` egress; consolidated §15 replant note; full local cargo gates; a manual 2-turn dogfood smoke on a real Claude model.

US-002, US-003, US-004 all depend only on a GO probe (US-001). US-003 (core) and US-004 (overlay new file) are file-disjoint and could run in parallel; US-002, US-003, US-005 all touch `core/src/chat_transport.rs` and/or `patch-surface.md` and must serialize relative to each other. US-005 joins everything; US-006 hardens.

## Scope

### In Scope
- A confirmation re-probe of `/v1/messages` (auth / signed emission / signed replay-before-`tool_result`), with a committed GO/NO-GO decision artifact + raw captures.
- A third `WireApi::AnthropicMessages` / `ModelWireRoute::AnthropicMessages` transport arm, `/v1/messages` recognition in `wire_route_for`, the `effective_wire_api` mapping (gated, degrade-to-chat), and the `client.rs` dispatch arm.
- A stricter `Feature::AnthropicSignedMessages` gate (default off) + resolver.
- Inbound: surface `thinking`+`signature` from the Messages SSE and persist the signature into `ResponseItem::Reasoning.encrypted_content`.
- Outbound (overlay): an Anthropic Messages request builder that replays the signed `thinking` block immediately before its `tool_use`, with `tool_result` in the following user message; bounded by the per-item byte cap (incl. signature bytes).
- Tests: parser signature-capture, request-builder ordering, routing/gate, a signed round-trip integration test across the tool loop, and a network-audit guard for `/v1/messages` egress.
- patch-surface §14 invariants (54+) + §15 replant note + Invariant 38 allowlist update; `audit_network_calls.sh` allowlist update.

### Out of Scope
- Any change to the `/responses` transport or to the unsigned `/chat/completions` reasoning capture/replay (it is the degrade-to fallback and stays as-is).
- A user-facing TUI redesign of reasoning/thinking rendering (reuse existing rendering).
- Building/landing any codex-rs transport code on a NO-GO probe result (→ D-003, defer).
- Migrating the existing `anthropic_models` flag (separate task); the signed sub-flag is additive.
- The codex release cut + version bump (separate `/publish-sandbox-patch` task); this plan ends at green local gates + a dogfood smoke.

## Risk Areas

- **Proxy strips/rewrites/rejects signatures (HIGH — the decisive gate).** Copilot is a proxy; if it does not faithfully relay Anthropic signatures (especially accepting a replayed signed `thinking` before a `tool_result`), the signed path is no better than unsigned at the cost of a permanent third transport. Mitigation: US-001 confirmation re-probe gates all codex-rs work; NO-GO → halt (D-003). The `effective_wire_api` degrade-to-chat arm means even a regression after ship falls back to the working unsigned path.
- **Tool-loop ordering (HIGH).** Anthropic requires the signed `thinking`→`tool_use` in one assistant message and `tool_result` in the next user message. If the builder detaches the `thinking` from its `tool_use`, emits it after the `tool_use`, or binds it to the wrong `tool_result`, the proxy/model rejects the turn (400 / signature-validation failure) — strictly worse than the order-free unsigned path. The builder must bind each reasoning item to the `function_call` that immediately follows it in the persisted stream (the adjacency the unsigned lifecycle already enforces at `chat_transport.rs:146-147`). Covered by the US-004 request-builder ordering test and the US-005 round-trip test.
- **Exhaustive-match fan-out (MEDIUM).** A third `WireApi`/`ModelWireRoute` variant forces a new arm at every `match` site across the workspace; missing one is a compile error (good) but the change touches many files. Mitigation: `cargo check --workspace` after US-002; the degrade-to-chat default keeps semantics safe.
- **Bounded model-visible context (MEDIUM).** Signatures are additive metadata; the replayed signed `thinking` must respect the no-item-over-10K-tokens rule. Mitigation: reuse `capped_reasoning_plaintext` and count signature bytes against the per-item budget; regression test feeding an oversized signed item.
- **Parser-placement churn (MEDIUM).** Extending core `anthropic_sse.rs` vs a new overlay parser is a real fork in the road (the two research agents disagreed). The plan recommends extending the existing core parser (less code, already plumbed, fork-owned). If Phase-4 review or impl finds the core edit widens conflict surface unacceptably, fall back to a new overlay `messages_sse.rs`. Either way the signature-capture behavior + tests are identical.
- **Permanent third-transport maintenance (MEDIUM, accepted).** +2 seams to replant per upstream rebase; justified only by a GO probe proving faithful signed continuity. Documented in the §15 replant note.
- **Nested 2-repo impl friction (MEDIUM).** Inner-submodule code + wrapper ledger in one logical change; `/implement-with-ralph` cannot express it. Mitigation: flag for the lead to drive a direct impl with the two-commit flow (Open Questions / Next Step).
- **Billing/quota on a second endpoint (LOW/UNKNOWN).** `/v1/messages` may bill or rate-limit differently. The US-001 probe should note observed quota behavior; auth itself is unchanged (same Copilot bearer + host).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (US-001):** A runnable extension of `D:/ExtRepos/copilot-thinking-probe/probe.mjs` POSTs an Anthropic Messages request to `api.githubcopilot.com/v1/messages` using the fork's exact Copilot auth/headers, runs a 2-turn flow (turn 1 captures signed `thinking`+`signature`; turn 2 replays the signed `thinking` block before a `tool_result`), and writes raw SSE/response captures to a **gitignored** path. Sensitive material (the `Authorization`/bearer token, any `ChatGPT-Account-Id`) is **never** committed.
- **AC2 (US-001):** A committed decision artifact `.ralph/jobs/codex-anthropic-native-messages-transport-for-signed-cot/probe-decision.md` records a GO/NO-GO verdict keyed to the three gates (auth accepted / `thinking`+`signature` emitted / signed thinking accepted on replay before `tool_result`), each with a **sanitized** raw-capture citation (secrets redacted); plus observed billing/quota behavior on `/v1/messages`. On NO-GO the artifact recommends D-003 and **no codex-rs code is modified**.
- **AC3 (US-002):** `WireApi::AnthropicMessages` is added (enum + `Display` → `"anthropicmessages"` + `Deserialize` + the `&["responses","chatcompletions"]` unknown-variant list) and `ModelWireRoute::AnthropicMessages` is added; `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` passes (every exhaustive `match wire_api`/`match route` site updated, including the `#[cfg(test)]` `proto_wire_api` helper at `config/src/thread_config/remote.rs:291-300`).
- **AC4 (US-002):** `wire_route_for` returns `ModelWireRoute::AnthropicMessages` for a row advertising `/v1/messages` **only when** `anthropic_models_resolved()` AND `anthropic_signed_messages_resolved()` are both true; otherwise it returns the prior result. Unit tests extend the `copilot_models_endpoint.rs:547-720` fixture pattern.
- **AC5 (US-002):** `effective_wire_api_gated` takes the signed flag as an **explicit parameter** (mirroring the existing `anthropic_enabled: bool` at `:68-72`, so the decision is unit-testable without process-global state). In US-002 it **degrades the `AnthropicMessages` route to `WireApi::ChatCompletions` unconditionally** (asserted by a unit test); the resolver read happens only at the `effective_wire_api` wrapper (`:64-66`). `Feature::AnthropicSignedMessages` is registered (`default_enabled:false`) with an `install_anthropic_signed_messages_gate`/`anthropic_signed_messages_resolved` pair (mirroring `install_anthropic_gate`/`anthropic_models_resolved`), installed at config-build in `core/src/config/mod.rs`.
- **AC6 (US-002):** The `client.rs` `WireApi::AnthropicMessages` dispatch arm exists and, in the skeleton, **delegates to `stream_chat_completions`** (runs the model unsigned, never panics) — so even if `anthropic_signed_messages` is enabled before US-005, the model path still works over the unsigned chat transport. `cargo check --workspace` passes. (US-005 replaces this stub with the real driver.)
- **AC7 (US-003):** A parser unit test feeds an Anthropic Messages SSE fixture with `content_block_delta` `thinking_delta` + `signature_delta` and asserts the reasoning text + `signature` are surfaced (no longer dropped at the former `_ => {}` arm), via the extended `TranslatedSseEvent`. A **multi-block** fixture (two `thinking`+`tool_use` blocks at different/out-of-order `index`es) asserts each `signature_delta` binds to its own block's `thinking` (no cross-binding) — the signature is keyed by content-block index.
- **AC8 (US-003):** A persistence test asserts the closing reasoning item yields `ResponseItem::Reasoning { content: Some([ReasoningText{..}]), encrypted_content: Some(<signature>) }`, that the open-before-delta / close-before-message lifecycle is unchanged from the unsigned path, and that with multiple reasoning blocks each persisted item carries its own signature bound to the correct following `function_call`.
- **AC9 (US-004):** A request-builder unit test feeds a persisted `ResponseItem` stream containing a `reasoning` item with `encrypted_content: Some(sig)` immediately followed by a `function_call` and its `function_call_output`, and asserts the emitted Anthropic `messages[]` places `{type:"thinking", thinking, signature}` then `{type:"tool_use", …}` in one assistant message and `{type:"tool_result", tool_use_id, …}` in the next user message. A reasoning item with `encrypted_content: None` emits **NO** `thinking` block (it is omitted, never an unsigned `thinking` block); a test asserts no unsigned `thinking` is emitted on the Messages path. (Unsigned continuity is the chat-completions transport's job, not this one.)
- **AC9b (US-004):** Request-builder fidelity beyond reasoning: tests assert the builder translates the system prompt → Anthropic top-level `system`, tools + `tool_choice` → the Anthropic `tools` schema, multiple parallel tool calls preserved with distinct `tool_use` ids, and a normal text-only turn → a valid `messages[]` with no `thinking`/`tool_use` blocks. Each has a fixture; the builder hard-errors (never silently drops) on a Responses feature it cannot represent, mirroring `build_chat_request_body` (Invariant 36).
- **AC10 (US-004 + US-003):** Bounded model-visible context for signed reasoning: a regression test feeds an oversized signed reasoning item and asserts the replayed `thinking` (plaintext text + signature bytes) is capped so no item exceeds the no-item-over-10K-tokens bound; AND that `core/src/context_manager/history.rs` token accounting for `ResponseItem::Reasoning{encrypted_content:Some(..), content:Some(..)}` counts the plaintext `content` (not only the opaque `encrypted_content`) so the bound holds in history estimation, not just at the request builder.
- **AC11 (US-005):** The real `WireApi::AnthropicMessages` dispatch arm builds the request via the overlay Messages builder, POSTs to `/v1/messages` with Copilot auth/headers, and streams the response through the (extended) `AnthropicSseParser` mapped to `ResponseEvent`s. A `stream_anthropic_messages` driver mirrors `stream_chat_completions`; `effective_wire_api_gated` is flipped to honor the signed flag (route to `WireApi::AnthropicMessages` when on).
- **AC12 (US-005):** A signed round-trip integration test (`core/suite` via `test_codex`, mock `/v1/messages` SSE) proves the full path: parse signed `thinking`+`signature` → persist into `encrypted_content` → replay → request body carries the signed `thinking` block before the `tool_use`, signature preserved end-to-end across a tool-call turn.
- **AC13 (US-006):** A §14 grep-guard invariant asserts the only Copilot inference paths emitted in source are `/chat/completions` and `/v1/messages`, and **Invariant 38**'s documented Copilot inference-path set is extended to include `/v1/messages`. The egress HOST `api.githubcopilot.com` is already allowed host-level (no path allowlist exists in `scripts/audit_network_calls.sh` to extend); `scripts/audit_network_calls.sh` still passes (no new host, no unaudited endpoint pattern).
- **AC14 (US-002/003/005, finalized US-006):** Every upstream-canonical edit hunk / new variant / new seam carries a `// SANDBOX PATCH:` marker (not a literal per-line marker), and `codex/docs/implementation/patch-surface.md` gains §14 invariant rows starting at **63** (next free; current max = 62 — do NOT reuse 54–62) each with an enforcing test/grep guard, plus a §15 replant note covering the enum/route/gate/dispatch seams.
- **AC15 (gates):** `cargo check --workspace` passes from `external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs`; `cargo test -p codex-core`, `cargo test -p codex-copilot`, `cargo test -p codex-model-provider`, and `cargo test -p codex-model-provider-info` pass (including all new tests) — run from `external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/`; `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` passes. (`just test -p <crate>` is the `AGENTS.override.md`-preferred form but the `[windows]` recipe can fail from a Git-Bash shell with exit 9009, so `cargo test -p` is the robust path here. The justfile lives at `external/repos/codex-patched/justfile`, not under `codex-rs/`.) `cargo build --release` and `cargo test --workspace` are deferred to CI / `/publish-sandbox-patch`.
- **AC16 (US-006):** A manual 2-turn dogfood smoke on a real Claude model with the signed sub-flag on demonstrates a tool-call turn completes and the signed `thinking` is accepted on replay. Because the central risk is live-proxy acceptance, the sub-flag stays **landed-dark** (not operator-recommended) until this live dogfood passes; if the operator defers it, the plan ships in an explicit "landed dark, not operator-usable" state with AC12 (mock round-trip) as the interim evidence and the deferral noted in `patch-surface.md`.

## Preliminary Story Decomposition

- **US-001** — Confirmation re-probe of `/v1/messages` (3 gates) + decision artifact. External `probe.mjs`; **GATE**; no codex edits. Small.
- **US-002** — Routing skeleton + signed sub-flag (all upstream seams; inert): 3rd `WireApi`/`ModelWireRoute` arm (+ the `#[cfg(test)]` `proto_wire_api` match in `remote.rs`), `/v1/messages` recognition in `wire_route_for`, `effective_wire_api` arm (degrades to chat unconditionally here, signed flag as explicit param), `Feature::AnthropicSignedMessages` + `install`/`resolved` pair + config-build install (`core/src/config/mod.rs`), model-cache identity key, `GatedModelsManager` filter, `synthesize_from_capabilities` default level, and a `client.rs` dispatch stub that delegates to `stream_chat_completions`. Medium.
- **US-003** — Inbound signed-SSE capture + signature persistence: surface `thinking_delta`/`signature_delta` (keyed by content-block index); persist into `encrypted_content`; history token-accounting for plaintext+signature. Core. Medium.
- **US-004** — Outbound Anthropic Messages request builder (overlay new file): signed `thinking`→`tool_use`→`tool_result` ordering, `encrypted_content:None`→omit (no unsigned thinking), system/tools/tool_choice/multi-tool/text-only fidelity, byte cap. **Uses its own fixtures** (constructs `ResponseItem::Reasoning{encrypted_content:Some(sig)}` directly) so it stays parallel-safe with US-003. Large.
- **US-005** — Dispatch wiring + signed round-trip: real `WireApi::AnthropicMessages` arm + `stream_anthropic_messages` driver + integration test. Medium.
- **US-006** — Harden/audit/verify: network-audit allowlist (Inv 38 + `audit_network_calls.sh`), consolidated §15 replant note, full local cargo gates, dogfood smoke. Small–Medium.

## Suggested Decomposition

This is a codex-submodule nested 2-repo build; most stages share `core/src/chat_transport.rs`, `core/src/client.rs`, and `patch-surface.md`, so execution is **mostly serial**. The one safe parallel pair is the core inbound-capture and the overlay request-builder (file-disjoint). The full build will most likely be driven by a single direct-impl member through the two-commit flow (see Next Step) rather than parallel Ralph jobs.

### Cluster: probe-gate
- Stories: US-001
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[]; exclusive=[`D:/ExtRepos/copilot-thinking-probe/probe.mjs`, `.ralph/jobs/codex-anthropic-native-messages-transport-for-signed-cot/probe-decision.md`]; risk=low
- `execution_mode` rationale: Touches only the external probe repo + a decision artifact; fully disjoint from codex source. It is the GO/NO-GO gate for every other cluster — nothing else may start until it returns GO.

### Cluster: routing-skeleton
- Stories: US-002
- Phase: 2
- Depends on: probe-gate
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`core/src/chat_transport.rs`, `core/src/client.rs`, `docs/implementation/patch-surface.md`]; exclusive=[`model-provider-info/src/lib.rs`, `protocol/src/openai_models.rs`, `config/src/thread_config/remote.rs`, `model-provider/src/copilot_models_endpoint.rs`, `model-provider/src/copilot/gated_models_manager.rs`, `features/src/lib.rs`, `model-provider/src/anthropic_gate.rs`, `core/src/config/mod.rs`]; risk=medium
- `execution_mode` rationale: Adds the enum/route/gate seams + a degrade-to-chat dispatch stub; compiles independently and is inert (always degrades to the working unsigned path), so it must land FIRST and alone — its `chat_transport.rs`/`client.rs`/`patch-surface.md` edits overlap the join cluster.

### Cluster: inbound-capture
- Stories: US-003
- Phase: 3
- Depends on: routing-skeleton
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`core/src/chat_transport.rs`, `docs/implementation/patch-surface.md`]; exclusive=[`core/src/chat_transport/anthropic_sse.rs`]; risk=medium
- `execution_mode` rationale: Surfaces the signature and persists it; serialized after routing-skeleton because both edit `core/src/chat_transport.rs` and the patch-surface ledger. File-disjoint from outbound-builder, so the two MAY run in parallel if a coordinator manages the shared `patch-surface.md` prepend.

### Cluster: outbound-builder
- Stories: US-004
- Phase: 3
- Depends on: probe-gate
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[]; exclusive=[`codex-rs-overlay/codex-copilot/src/anthropic_messages.rs` (new), `codex-rs-overlay/codex-copilot/src/payload.rs` (exports only)]; risk=low
- `execution_mode` rationale: A new overlay file (zero upstream conflict surface). It defines its OWN test fixtures (constructing `ResponseItem::Reasoning{encrypted_content:Some(sig)}` directly rather than depending on the US-003 parser), so it is genuinely file-disjoint from inbound-capture and can run in parallel with it. It does not touch routing, so it only needs the probe GO. Safer fallback if parallelism is undesired: serialize after inbound-capture.

### Cluster: dispatch-join
- Stories: US-005
- Phase: 4
- Depends on: routing-skeleton, inbound-capture, outbound-builder
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`core/src/chat_transport.rs`, `core/src/client.rs`, `docs/implementation/patch-surface.md`]; exclusive=[`core/src/suite/<signed_messages_roundtrip>.rs` (new test)]; risk=medium
- `execution_mode` rationale: Replaces the dispatch stub with the real arm + `stream_anthropic_messages` driver and adds the round-trip integration test; depends on all three Phase-2/3 clusters and re-touches the shared core files, so it serializes last among the build clusters.

### Cluster: harden-verify
- Stories: US-006
- Phase: 5
- Depends on: dispatch-join
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`docs/implementation/patch-surface.md`]; exclusive=[`scripts/audit_network_calls.sh`]; risk=low
- `execution_mode` rationale: Network-audit allowlist + consolidated §15 replant note + full local cargo gates + dogfood smoke; runs after the join is complete so the audit reflects the final egress surface.

Parallel handoff (conceptual staging only — NOT the recommended vehicle; see Next Step / the lead Note, which mandate a direct nested-2-repo impl rather than `/implement-with-ralph`): the clusters above map to `--suggested-decomposition .ralph/jobs/codex-anthropic-native-messages-transport-for-signed-cot/suggested-decomposition.json`.

> Note (lead): This is a **codex-submodule nested 2-repo** change (inner `codex-patched` Rust + codex-wrapper `patch-surface.md`). `/implement-with-ralph`'s single-repo/one-worktree/one-branch model cannot express a nested 2-repo change; per codexu AGENTS.md ("Codex submodule impls touching BOTH inner code and wrapper docs … do a direct impl with the two-commit flow") this most likely needs a **direct impl** driven story-by-story with `cargo check --workspace` (Phase 5a) + code review + lockstep `patch-surface.md` (Phase 5b), NOT a parallel Ralph fan-out. The suggested-decomposition above is the conceptual staging; treat US-001 (probe) as a hard gate before any Rust stage. Also: US-001 targets an external repo (`D:/ExtRepos/copilot-thinking-probe`), so even a single autonomous chain must run it (and write `probe-decision.md`) before any codex edit.

## Next Step

This is a **codex-submodule nested 2-repo change** (inner `codex-patched` Rust + codex-wrapper `patch-surface.md`), so the standard `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan` auto-chain is **deliberately NOT provided** — its single-repo/one-worktree/one-branch model would silently drop either the inner submodule commit or the wrapper ledger/pointer commit (codexu AGENTS.md: "Dual-repo plans don't chain into `/implement-with-ralph` blindly"). **US-001 (probe) is a hard gate before any Rust lands.**

Recommended impl vehicle (lead decision at handoff): a **direct, story-by-story impl** with the two-commit flow:

1. Run **US-001** first against `D:/ExtRepos/copilot-thinking-probe` and commit `probe-decision.md`. On **NO-GO, STOP** (→ D-003; no Rust).
2. On **GO**, implement US-002 → US-006 in order (US-003 ∥ US-004 optional) inside an inner-submodule worktree (`external/repos/codex-patched/.worktrees/<task>` off `sandbox-patches`), running `cargo metadata --no-deps` preflight + `cargo check --workspace` (Phase 5a) + `cargo test -p <crate>` + code review + lockstep `patch-surface.md` (Phase 5b) per stage.
3. Commit **inner submodule first**, then the **codex-wrapper** commit recording the new inner gitlink + `patch-surface.md`, then the **codexu pointer bump** — three commits across two nested repos.

Alternatively the lead may split US-001 (external probe repo) and the codex build into separate repo-scoped jobs. Do not run a single `/implement-with-ralph` over the whole plan.

After merging, clean up the plan worktree with `/plan-with-ralph cleanup codex-anthropic-native-messages-transport-for-signed-cot`.
